name: 2108 S. Prairie Avenue — the coach house of 2108 and 2110, one building divided on their lot line (district draft; refined by T-1937)

function.note: The 1911 sheet reads 'The north half of a 2-storey brick stable (crossed) on the alley, one building with 2110's half (ruling r35-2108-2110-coach-house)' and 'The south half of the 2-storey brick stable (crossed) on the alley, divided from 2108's half on the lot line (ruling r35-2108-2110-coach-house)'. A "good brick barn" in the to-let notices of February 1904, so its 1904 use is attested. One building, not two (census ruling r35-2108-2110-coach-house): the sheet draws a single two-storey brick stable across the alley end of both lots, divided on the lot line; Mark Kimball's coach house spanned both lots when Rees bought 2110 from him in 1888, Rees taking the south half behind a new party wall, and the February 1904 to-let notice for 2108 includes a good brick barn. The draft fills the two traced halves as one envelope and stands the lot line through it as that party wall.

research_note: A DISTRICT DRAFT (T-2351, the owner's district pass of 2026-10-08): a serviceable first model, complete from the street, the walks, the alley and the air, that T-1937 refines in place under this same id. Written by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py from the sheet 35 trace (s35fp-2108-b2 and s35fp-2110-b2, filled as one building), the T-1842 census (s35-2108-rear, s35-2110-rear) and the T-1837 register row frontage-35-065; every height, roof, opening and feature is the draft rules' reconstruction (data/components/prairie_1904/draft_prairie_1904.json; liberty L-draft-prairie-20-22-west-2351).

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1842 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

draft_elevation.note: RECONSTRUCTED by the draft rules, family row 'service' overlaid with the frontage row: The Mark Kimball house, empty and to let in the spring of 1904 (not W. W. Kimball's at 1801): the register's 'two-storey/basement brick house with simple cornice/roof' as a flat roof behind a plain cornice over the 2B body and its rear range. The to-let notice calls it a stone front and the sheet colours it brick; the draft keeps the sheet's brick, and T-1921 chooses. Heights are the rules' starting values inside RECONSTRUCTION-RULES.md's ranges; bays, entrance side, chimneys and dormers are counts the family rules choose, and the seed 1070065418 only tints the fabric inside +-6 %.
